body:
## Pull request overview Improves the mobile detail-page experience across the layout shell, action toolbars, and detail views by removing duplicated sidebar toggles, reducing action button clutter, and making detail fields use screen width more effectively. **Changes:** - Hide AppShell’s sidebar trigger on smaller viewports to avoid duplicating the AppHeader mobile trigger. - Make `action:bar` adapt its inline action count on mobile via `useIsMobile()` and a new `mobileMaxVisible` schema prop. - Adjust DetailView header actions and DetailSection grid breakpoints for a cleaner mobile layout. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailView.tsx | Hides some header actions on small screens and mirrors them into the “More Actions” dropdown. | | packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailSection.tsx | Updates responsive grid column breakpoints (md→sm) to use width more effectively on smaller devices. | | packages/layout/src/AppShell.tsx | Hides AppShell’s built-in sidebar trigger on mobile to prevent duplicate toggles with AppHeader. | | packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-bar.tsx | Adds mobile-aware `maxVisible` logic and introduces `mobileMaxVisible` schema support. |
Comments suppressed due to low confidence (2) **packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-bar.tsx:50** * `mobileMaxVisible` is added to the schema interface, but it isn't exposed in the ComponentRegistry config (`inputs` / `defaultProps`). That means schema-driven tooling/designers can't set it and the default isn't documented alongside `maxVisible`. Add an input entry (and optionally a default prop) for `mobileMaxVisible` to keep the registry metadata in sync with the renderer behavior. ``` /** Maximum visible inline actions before overflow into "More" menu (default: 3) */ maxVisible?: number; /** Maximum visible inline actions on mobile devices (default: 1). Desktop uses maxVisible instead. */ mobileMaxVisible?: number; ``` **packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailView.tsx:554** * These changes introduce new mobile-only behavior (Share/Edit/Inline Edit moved into the More Actions dropdown and hidden inline). There are existing `DetailView` tests, but none assert the new mobile menu items exist and trigger the correct handlers when the inline buttons are hidden. Add/adjust tests to cover the dropdown items (and the `sm:hidden`/`sm:inline-flex` split) to prevent regressions. ``` {/* Inline Edit Toggle - hidden on mobile, accessible via more menu */} {inlineEdit && ( {isInlineEditing ? t('detail.saveChanges') : t('detail.editFieldsInline')} )} {/* Share Button - hidden on mobile, accessible via more menu */} {t('detail.share')} {/* Edit Button - hidden on mobile, accessible via more menu */} {schema.showEdit && ( {t('detail.editRecord')} )} {/* More Actions Menu */} {t('detail.moreActions')} {/* Mobile-only: Share, Edit, Inline Edit */} {t('detail.share')} {schema.showEdit && ( {t('detail.edit')} )} {inlineEdit && ( {isInlineEditing ? t('detail.save') : t('detail.editInline')} )} ```

Hiding the only built-in <SidebarTrigger> below `md` makes the sidebar impossible to open on mobile for AppShell consumers that do not render their own mobile trigger in `navbar` (e.g. AppSchemaRenderer when `navbar` is undefined, and AppShell Storybook stories). Consider gating this behind an explicit AppShell prop (e.g. `hideTriggerOnMobile`) or keeping the trigger visible by default and letting apps opt into hiding it when they provide their own header trigger.
```suggestion
          <SidebarTrigger className="-ml-1 inline-flex" />
          <div className="w-px h-4 bg-border mx-1 sm:mx-2 block" />
```

`useIsMobile()` relies on `window.matchMedia()` (and `addEventListener`) without a guard. Now that ActionBar always calls it, environments that don't provide matchMedia (unit tests, some non-browser runtimes) will throw during effect execution. Either make `useIsMobile` resilient when `window.matchMedia` is missing, or provide a global matchMedia mock in the test setup so ActionBar rendering can't crash.

This breakpoint change (md→sm) will break existing unit tests that assert `md:grid-cols-2` / `md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3` for auto-layout. Update `DetailSection.test.tsx` expectations to match the new responsive classes (`sm:grid-cols-2`, etc.) so CI reflects the intended behavior.
